record.paper_title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter
record.original_question: The current SK theory explains phase-transition pressures using only a simplified electrostatic interaction and neglects additional contributions to the intermolecular or interparticle potential energy. How should the theory be refined so that more components of the interparticle potential energy are included, and does incorporating those missing potential terms materially reduce the discrepancy between predicted and measured high-pressure phase-transition pressures?

evidence.quote: the second "source of problems" is represented by the fact that the SK theory neglects the contribution of various non-electrostatic components to the overall intermolecular potential.
On the purely theoretical side,in would be necessary to refine the theory with the inclusion of the contribution of more components to the interparticle potential energy.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a semiclassical model (the Siringo–Kocik / SK-type framework) for predicting structural phase-transition pressures in dense molecular or atomic matter, in which each particle is treated as a polarizable charge distribution and the only interaction energy retained is a simplified electrostatic (Coulomb / multipole-screened) potential V_es(r) between particles. Within this model, the predicted high-pressure phase-transition pressures P_th differ systematically from experimentally measured values P_exp.

Let the full pair interparticle potential admit a decomposition

    V_total(r) = V_es(r) + V_exch(r) + V_disp(r) + V_ind(r) + V_rep(r) + ...,

where V_exch is the exchange (Pauli) contribution, V_disp the dispersion (van der Waals) contribution, V_ind the induction (polarization) contribution, and V_rep the short-range repulsive core, each treated at an appropriate semiclassical level.

Problem. 
(a) Formulate an extension of the semiclassical theory in which the equation of state and the criterion determining structural phase-transition pressures are derived from V_total rather than from V_es alone. Specify how each non-electrostatic component should be modeled (functional form, parameters, and how it enters the free energy / stability criterion) so that the resulting theory remains semiclassical and tractable.
(b) Determine quantitatively whether the inclusion of the non-electrostatic components V_exch, V_disp, V_ind, V_rep materially reduces the discrepancy |P_th − P_exp| for a representative set of high-pressure phase transitions; in particular, identify which of these components dominate the correction and obtain bounds or estimates for the improved theoretical pressures.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific follow-up work was located that systematically refines the SK semiclassical theory by incorporating exchange, dispersion, induction, and short-range repulsive contributions and demonstrates a quantitative reduction of the discrepancy with measured high-pressure phase-transition pressures. The problem appears to remain an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter
status_evidence.snippet: Lists refinement of the interparticle potential by including more non-electrostatic components as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The refinement was posed as an open problem and no resolution was identified in subsequent literature.
